headline: Cloning Any Website in One Prompt, Using Live Browser Data
lede: The standard AI approach to copying a website begins with a screenshot — a lossy, static image that forces the model to guess at fonts, colours, and spacing. A new open-source skill for Claude Code, Anthropic's terminal-based coding assistant, abandons that workaround: it routes a live Chrome browser session directly at the target, pulling computed styles and asset paths from the source itself. The result collapses what was a multi-step, imprecise process into a single natural-language prompt.
body:
The conventional screenshot-to-code pipeline has always worked at one remove from the truth. A developer named @JCodesMore built a skill for **Claude Code** that discards that crutch entirely. Rather than feeding the model a JPEG and asking it to reverse-engineer the design, the skill opens a *Chrome MCP* connection — a live channel into the browser's rendering engine — where computed *CSS*, font manifests, colour tokens, and animation parameters are all directly legible.

The workflow unfolds in automated stages. The skill navigates to the target, extracts the visual foundation — typeface stack, colour palette, layout grid — while capturing reference screenshots, then spawns parallel sub-agents to reconstruct separate page sections concurrently. A final pass reviews their output, merges it, and delivers a working clone. One natural-language prompt triggers the entire sequence.

The capability sits at an uncomfortable ethical boundary. Automated cloning tools have existed for decades — *HTTrack*, Wget's mirror mode — but lowering the skill threshold to a single prompt meaningfully expands who can deploy them and at what scale. Lookalike phishing pages, IP-infringing storefronts, and scraped brand sites are the obvious threat vectors. The tool's most prominent amplifier on LinkedIn acknowledged as much, noting he was not endorsing intellectual-property theft, and pointing to more defensible uses: scaffolding internal dashboards, prototyping UI layouts without boilerplate, or benchmarking a competitor's design language.

What distinguishes this from earlier screenshot pipelines is the *MCP* layer. Model Context Protocol — an open standard published by Anthropic — defines how Claude Code calls external tools as part of its reasoning loop. A Chrome MCP server exposes the browser as a queryable instrument: the model can inspect the *DOM*, read computed style rules, and retrieve asset manifests rather than squinting at pixels. That architectural shift — from static image to live debugger — is more significant than any particular clone it produces.

concepts.definition: Anthropic's command-line AI coding assistant, invoked from a terminal rather than a chat interface. It can plan, write, and execute code, call external tools via MCP, and coordinate multiple sub-agents — making it suitable for multi-step automation tasks like website cloning.

A Model Context Protocol server that exposes a live Chrome browser instance to an AI model as a callable tool. Rather than receiving a static screenshot, the model can navigate pages, query the DOM, and read computed styles in real time.

An open standard published by Anthropic that defines how AI models invoke external tools and services during a reasoning session. It standardises the interface between a model and capabilities like file systems, browsers, APIs, and databases.

The web language that controls visual presentation — fonts, colours, spacing, and animation — as applied to HTML elements. Computed CSS is the final, resolved set of style rules the browser actually applies after all stylesheets and inheritance are processed.

The browser's structured, in-memory representation of a web page, which makes every element — text, image, button — programmatically accessible. Reading the DOM directly gives an AI model the page's actual structure rather than a visual approximation.

Multiple AI agent instances invoked concurrently to work on separate subtasks — here, different sections of a page — whose outputs are merged afterward. Running agents in parallel reduces the total time compared to processing each section sequentially.

A long-established, free command-line utility that recursively downloads an entire website — pages, images, stylesheets — to a local folder for offline viewing. It is a precursor to AI-assisted cloning but requires manual configuration and produces static copies without intelligent reconstruction.
